sources.citation: Gomes, Armindo Jaime (Arjago). n.d. O poder da autoridade tradicional em Benguela - duas realidades etno-históricas na mesma perspectiva. BUALA (web article, section 'Vou lá visitar'), accessed 2026-09-21.
sources.note: No phonology content. Ethno-historical essay on the ekula age-class institution and traditional authority; olundombe appears only as isolated terms (ekula, ocoto, ekwenje, Okufekalã, Makunga, Okuyanga) in plain Portuguese-based spelling with no tone or stress marking; bibliography cites no linguistic work on Ndombe. (HTML looked up through the compiler gate, 49 KB, kept only in the work dir.)

sources.citation: Menezes, Bernardo Kessongo. 2020. A Toponímia da Região de Benguela: das memórias coloniais à era contemporânea (século XX-XXI) [title page: Séc. XIX-XX]. Tese de Doutoramento em História, FCSH, Universidade Nova de Lisboa. hdl 10362/107814.
sources.note: Nothing on Ndombe. Searched the 476k-char text for ndombe/Vandombe/undombe/Dombe Grande (17 hits, all ethnonym/toponym/history) and for acento (0), tónic (0), tonal (1: 'tonalidades' figurative), tom/tons/tonolog (0), fonolog (4: Umbundu toponyms 'gráfica e fonologicamente violados', nasalisation kept by speakers), fonétic (7, general method), prosód/entoação/sílaba tónica (0). No statement about stress or tone in any language, let alone olundombe.

sources.citation: Gomes, Armindo Jaime. 2016. Fundamentos da ekula no poder tradicional mundombe. Mulemba: Revista Angolana de Ciências Sociais 6(12): 179-202. DOI 10.4000/mulemba.1087.
sources.note: No phonology content. Ethno-historical article; cites isolated olundombe lexical items (otchombo 'kilombo', elisululu, omutapi vs. olukwandu ohutapi, matemba/eholo/etumba, vakwetuva/ukwetuva) and a short oath formula ('Yeveleli!.. Catete, ocanu cenu etuva') in plain orthography without tone or stress marks; states Umbundu sociocultural pressure on the Ndombe since colonial times.

sources.citation: Jordan, Linda. 2015. A Comparison of Five Speech Varieties of Southwestern Angola: Comparing OluHumbe, OluCilenge, OluKwandu, OluNgendelengo, and OluKuvale in the Kamucuio Municipality, Namibe Province. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2015-017.
sources.note: Ndombe language not covered ('Ndombe Grande' appears only as a place name); explicitly says 'Tone is not covered in this paper'; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Gomes, Armindo Jaime. 2014. Mundombe do «Dombe» ou Ndombe do Mundombe?.. Mulemba: Revista Angolana de Ciências Sociais 4(8): 77-100. DOI 10.4000/mulemba.401 (CORE/OpenEdition PDF)
sources.note: Nothing; onomastics/identity paper. States the Vandombe of Dombe Grande today mostly speak Umbundu, with olundombe surviving residually in family contexts, and that colonial authors treated olundombe as a cross between Umbundu and Olucilenge.

sources.note: Page concerns zone R subgrouping (Nkumbi, Wambo, Herero, Umbundu); Ndombe appears in the volume only in the Guthrie/Maho code list (R12); nothing on Ndombe prosody.

sources.citation: [Homburger, L.] 1925. Mission Rohan-Chabot. Angola et Rhodesia (1912-1914). Tome III, fascicule 1: Linguistique. Le groupe sud-ouest des langues bantoues. Paris: Imprimerie nationale / Librairie Paul Geuthner. x+176 pp. (Note preliminaire signed L. Homburger.)
sources.note: Nothing for Ndombe. The only Ndombe material is the numeral column on p. 133: 1 mosi, 2 baari, 3 tantu, 4 kuana, 5 taanu, 6 pandu, 7 pandu baari, 8 ecianana [c-hacek], 9 kieya, 10 kumi. p. 134 discusses numeral syntax for Bailundu/Kwambi only. The comparative phonology (ch. III, pp. 85-105) and 'recueil de synonymes en sept parlers' cover Kwambi, Bailundu, Ganguela, Nyaneka, Ndonga, Luyi, Kimbundu; the volume's single use of 'accent' (p. 86) is a general remark that consonant correspondences are not influenced by accent.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1922. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 2. Oxford: Clarendon Press. (Group X, South-West Africa languages, phonology/prefix commentary)
sources.note: Group X commentary mentions Ndombe (no. 93) only for the class 6 prefix Ba-; no statement on stress or accent for Ndombe.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 1. Oxford: Clarendon Press. (Ndombe = language no. 93, pp. 350-351 footnote, p. 780 supplementary vocabulary, pp. 800-801 bibliography note)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives only 8 Ndombe words (p. 780) and calls it a 'scarcely known tongue' / 'as yet scarcely illustrated' (p. 800-801); his 'Ndombe or Kwando, 93a Koroka' is placed on the Mossamedes coast and said to be 'very similar to Olunyaneka'.
